title: OutboxStore::mark_failed not atomic - message/outbox mismatch risk
description:
File: /home/mark/WORK/KITH/crates/kith-store/src/outbox.rs, lines 123-145

The mark_failed() function performs three separate SQL operations:
1. Line 128: UPDATE messages SET delivery_state = 'failed'
2. Line 135: UPDATE outbox SET last_error (redundant, about to delete)
3. Line 141: DELETE FROM outbox

Each is a separate execute() call without explicit transaction wrapping. If the process crashes after step 1 but before step 3, the message is marked 'failed' but the outbox row still exists. On recovery, the next attempt to deliver will try again, creating inconsistent state.

CORRECT BEHAVIOR: All three operations must be in the same transaction to ensure atomicity. If delivery is 'failed', the outbox entry must be deleted; and vice versa.

IMPACT: Data inconsistency — outbox entries may not match message delivery_state, breaking assumptions in retry logic.

NOTE: The UPDATE at line 135 is also redundant since the DELETE at line 141 will remove the row anyway.
